title: Observability & SRE
summary: The vocabulary of running prod — observability (logs, metrics, traces, OpenTelemetry), SRE practices (SLIs/SLOs/error budgets, alerting, on-call, postmortems), reliability engineering (chaos engineering, capacity planning), and the AI-era observability frontier.

volatileChapters.reason: Observability vendor landscape (Datadog, Honeycomb, New Relic, Splunk) competes on features each quarter; Prometheus storage ecosystem (Cortex, Mimir, Thanos, VictoriaMetrics) evolves rapidly; AIOps capabilities ship continuously.
LLM observability is the fastest-moving subdiscipline — new vendors (LangSmith, LangFuse, Arize, Helicone) appear quarterly; OTel GenAI semantic conventions are draft.

inspiredBy.title: Observability Engineering + Google SRE Book + SRE Workbook

chapters.title: Observability ≠ Monitoring
chapters.summary: The conceptual baseline — observability vs monitoring (known-unknowns vs unknown-unknowns), the three pillars and four golden signals, RED and USE methods, cardinality, wide events, and the cost of cardinality.

chapters.title: Logs, Metrics, Traces
chapters.summary: The three classical pillars — structured logging, log levels and aggregation, the metric types (counter, gauge, histogram, summary), and the anatomy of distributed traces (span, trace context, parent linkage).

chapters.title: OpenTelemetry
chapters.summary: The vendor-neutral observability framework — the specification, per-language SDKs, auto vs manual instrumentation, the Collector pipeline (receiver/processor/exporter), semantic conventions, sampling decisions, and OTLP.

chapters.title: SLI / SLO / Error Budgets
chapters.summary: The core SRE math — picking SLIs that measure user happiness, SLO targets and their downtime budgets, error budgets and their policies, burn-rate alerting (multi-window multi-burn), and the 100% trap.

chapters.title: Designing for Reliability
chapters.summary: Patterns that survive failure — redundancy and N+1, bulkheads, circuit breakers, load shedding, graceful degradation, timeouts, retries with backoff and jitter, idempotency, rate limiting, and throttling.

chapters.title: Alerting and On-Call
chapters.summary: Wakeup engineering — symptom vs cause alerts, pages vs tickets, alert fatigue, runbooks, rotation patterns (primary/secondary/follow-the-sun), severity levels, auto-remediation, and on-call compensation.

chapters.title: Incident Response
chapters.summary: Running an incident — Incident Commander, Communications and Operations leads, scribe role, severity levels, war room hygiene, status page communication, hand-offs across shifts, and declaring vs closing an incident.

chapters.title: Postmortems and Learning
chapters.summary: Learning from failure — blameless postmortems, the five-whys critique, contributing factors and system thinking, timelines, action items and their half-life, postmortem reviews, near-miss postmortems, and latent failures.

chapters.title: Toil, Automation, and Capacity
chapters.summary: The SRE economic engine — toil definition + budget (50% cap), eliminating vs automating, capacity planning and headroom, load testing in prod, right-sizing, cost vs reliability, and the toil-reduction tactics.

chapters.title: Chaos and Resilience Engineering
chapters.summary: Disciplined experimentation in production — the steady-state hypothesis, blast radius, game days, Chaos Monkey lineage, Litmus and Chaos Mesh, failure injection types, resilience vs reliability, and anti-fragility.

chapters.title: Distributed Tracing in Practice
chapters.summary: Production tracing — context propagation, W3C Trace Context, baggage, sampling strategies (head, tail, probabilistic, adaptive), span tagging, trace-to-log and trace-to-metric correlation, and trace analysis.

chapters.title: The Tools Landscape
chapters.summary: The observability vendor and OSS landscape — Prometheus + Cortex/Mimir/Thanos/VictoriaMetrics, Grafana, Datadog, Honeycomb, New Relic, Loki, Tempo, Jaeger, Splunk, Elastic Stack, AIOps, and the OTel vs lock-in calculus.

chapters.title: Observability in the AI Era
chapters.summary: The new frontier — LLM tracing (prompt → tokens → response), agent observability (tool calls, retries), token cost telemetry, evaluation as observability, hallucination detection, vector DB metrics, multi-step agent traces, RAG observability, and the LLM-observability vendor landscape.
